ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, point C is at the lower right and has a right-angle mark, point A is above C, point B is at the lower left; AC is the vertical side, BC is the base, AB is the hypotenuse. Therefore AB is the hypotenuse of the right triangle, AC is the opposite side of angle B, and BC is the adjacent side of angle B. Reasoning: It is known that ∠C = 90°, AB = 5, AC = 4. By the Pythagorean theorem, BC^2 = AB^2 - AC^2 = 5^2 - 4^2 = 25 - 16 = 9, so BC = 3. For angle B, tan B = opposite side/adjacent side = AC/BC = 4/3.
